To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
auditory cortex plasticity is maintained throughout development, and that intensive training can overcome developmental deficits in auditory cortex function.

1) the auditory cortex of rats reared in the presence of noise during the critical period is impaired in processing temporal cues; 2) the impaired temporal processing can be restored by training; and 3) the restoration of normal temporal processing persists long after training cessation.
“Enduring deficits in cortical temporal processing can be restored by training.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of early auditory training on the development and plasticity of the auditory cortex.
how experience can shape the development of the auditory system and how this process can be modified.
how the brain develops and adapts, and with how it can be trained to improve its functioning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
auditory cortex plasticity is not restricted to the developmental critical period, that it can be elicited by training, and that this plasticity is not limited to the auditory system.
the auditory cortex of the developing brain is capable of reorganizing itself in response to intensive training.
the critical period is not fixed but rather a flexible window of opportunity that can be extended or shortened depending on the nature of the training.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of cortical temporal processing can be modified by environmental factors and that this modification is reversible by training.
the auditory cortex is capable of plastic reorganization in response to intensive training, but only if training is initiated during the critical period.
the auditory cortex is capable of substantial reorganization in response to training, and that this reorganization can persist for a long time after the training has ended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adult brain retains the ability to re-normalize the representation of sensory information in the presence of intensive and prolonged training.
it is possible to overcome developmental deficits by intensive training.
the auditory cortex is capable of reorganizing its neural circuitry in order to restore normal function.
